symptom: Windows cancellation, timeout and output-limit report process_cleanup_failed after the owned child has actually exited.
direct_cause: Force timer launches a second taskkill while the first asynchronous tree cleanup is still pending; a late taskkill failure attempts to kill an already exited child.
class_root: The bounded process owner does not serialize teardown operations or recognize an observed exited child at the Windows fallback boundary.
affected_population: Windows process cleanup under taskkill latency
internal_only_reason: Node child lifecycle and Nomi bounded-owner implementation are directly reproduced with real local fixture children; no inference or external behavior is involved.
invariants: At most one teardown operation is pending for a child.
An observed exited child does not become a cleanup failure merely because a late taskkill returns nonzero.
A still-running unkillable child retains process_cleanup_failed.
Grace expiry during a pending teardown retains a force request; settlement must service that request sequentially if the child is still live.
Terminal settlement prevents any new force request; late child close still updates close evidence. A final cleanup failure never authorizes a later PID-based force operation.

door_reduction.why_not: Media probe, decode, ffmpeg import and export are distinct consumers of the same bounded process owner.

generality_proof: Serialize the shared cleanup owner for all stop reasons and consumers, with explicit positive exit evidence for fallback completion.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own stop escalation without overlapping async teardown.
Recognize exited children and fail closed when live cleanup cannot succeed.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Actual import lifecycle integration exercises caller cancellation and quit.
Timeout, output-limit and abort real-child regressions.

recurrence.reason: Every Windows asynchronous taskkill longer than escalation grace can race another teardown.
same_class_scan: Inspected importTranscodeLifecycle integration and mediaProbe process owner tests
Inspected shared export and probe consumers

prevention.invariant: Only one cleanup operation owns a child at a time; fallback uses positive exit evidence.
prevention.failure_mode: Unconfirmed live process cleanup still fails visibly.
prevention.strategy: Guard escalation against a pending teardown and inspect child exitCode/signalCode before direct kill fallback.

legacy_paths.rationale: Overlapping force escalation is replaced in the existing owner; no alternative runner.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency upgrade; reuse existing shared publication contract.

migration: No user data changes; existing process clients retain their error and cancellation contracts.
residual_risks: Only owned fixture child processes are terminated during validation.
Independent review found and required the delayed graceful completion population, not only a first cleanup that kills the child.
